sentences.en: When the Democratic presidential nomination process begins tomorrow in South Carolina, the question is not who will win,
sentences.zh: 当民主党总统提名程序明天在南卡罗来纳州开始时，问题不在于谁会赢，

sentences.en: but whether President Biden can fix his growing problem with Black voters.
sentences.zh: 而在于拜登总统能否解决他在黑人选民中日益严重的问题。
我的同事玛雅·金为您解读。
今天是2月2日，星期五。

sentences.en: So, Maya, after weeks of covering the Republican presidential nomination process in Iowa and then New Hampshire,
sentences.zh: 那么，玛雅，在报道了数周爱荷华州和新罕布什尔州的共和党总统提名程序之后，

sentences.en: we are now officially ready to turn to the Democratic nomination process.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正式转向民主党的提名程序。

sentences.en: And that begins in South Carolina, not where it used to begin, which was in Iowa, along with the Republicans starting there.
sentences.zh: 它始于南卡罗来纳州，而不是像过去那样从爱荷华州开始，共和党人也是从那里开始的。

sentences.en: And just to begin, remind us why South Carolina is going first this year.
sentences.zh: 首先，请提醒我们为什么南卡罗来纳州今年排在第一位。

sentences.en: So, this process really started four years ago when Black voters in South Carolina turned out in large numbers to vote for then-candidate Biden,
sentences.zh: 这个过程其实始于四年前，当时南卡罗来纳州的黑人选民大量投票支持当时的候选人拜登，
有效地拯救了他的竞选活动。

sentences.en: He was really trailing in Iowa and in New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 他当时在爱荷华州和新罕布什尔州确实落后。
没错。

sentences.en: And it was when he got to South Carolina that all of these Black voters, seeing him as really the most pragmatic option, turned out in these large numbers to vote for him.
sentences.zh: 正是当他到达南卡罗来纳州时，所有这些黑人选民认为他是最务实的选择，于是大量投票支持他。

sentences.en: And he took that momentum from South Carolina to Super Tuesday, where he won pretty overwhelmingly.
sentences.zh: 他带着从南卡罗来纳州获得的势头进入了“超级星期二”，并以压倒性优势获胜。

sentences.en: And then, of course, was then the Democratic Party's nominee for president.
sentences.zh: 当然，他随后成为了民主党的总统候选人。
没错。

sentences.en: And Biden's very explicit about this and proud of it.
sentences.zh: 拜登对此非常明确，也引以为豪。
他经常说，
南卡罗来纳州的黑人选民

sentences.en: saved, revived my primary campaign, and they are the reason I'm president.
sentences.zh: 拯救并复兴了我的初选竞选，他们是我成为总统的原因。

sentences.en: He is not quiet about the role that South Carolina has played in his life and certainly in his political livelihood.
sentences.zh: 他从不避讳南卡罗来纳州在他个人生活，尤其是政治生涯中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: President Biden really points to South Carolina and Black voters here as a really key part of his coalition.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统确实将南卡罗来纳州和这里的黑人选民视为他联盟中非常关键的一部分。

sentences.en: And it's the reason why he openly says he asked the Democratic Party to put South Carolina first in the order of early primary states,
sentences.zh: 这也是他公开表示要求民主党将南卡罗来纳州排在早期初选州首位的原因，

sentences.en: putting Black voters, Black Americans, in the driver's seat, being the first Democrats in the country to decide who they want to be president.
sentences.zh: 让黑人选民、美国黑人掌握主动权，成为全国第一批决定他们想要谁担任总统的民主党人。

sentences.en: And there's not a lot of suspense around what's going to happen tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天会发生什么并没有太多悬念。

sentences.en: The primary here in South Carolina is largely uncompetitive.
sentences.zh: 南卡罗来纳州的初选基本上没有竞争。

sentences.en: It's very clear that Biden will be victorious.
sentences.zh: 很明显，拜登将会获胜。

sentences.en: However, we're not really watching for the election results.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们关注的重点其实不是选举结果。

sentences.en: We're more looking at what's happening outside of them and some of the dynamics that have caused Democrats to really hone in on South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 我们更多是在观察选举之外发生的事情，以及导致民主党人真正聚焦于南卡罗来纳州的一些动态。

sentences.en: And it's because they've identified in polling and focus groups and conversations a real problem with one of the key coalitions that they will need in November,
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们在民调、焦点小组和对话中发现，他们11月大选所需的核心联盟之一存在真正的问题，
那就是黑人选民。

sentences.en: And that's why South Carolina, for the last several weeks, has been something of a laboratory or a proving ground of sorts for Democrats as they try to form a message
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么过去几周南卡罗来纳州成了民主党人的某种实验室或试验场，他们试图形成一种信息，

sentences.en: that would excite and galvanize Black voters, not just here, but across the country.
sentences.zh: 能够激励和动员黑人选民，不仅是在这里，而且是在全国范围内。

sentences.en: Democrats' hope here is that what they learn from Black voters in South Carolina is applicable to Black voters in other parts of the country,
sentences.zh: 民主党人在这里的希望是，他们从南卡罗来纳州黑人选民身上学到的东西，能够适用于全国其他地区的黑人选民，

sentences.en: cities like Detroit, Milwaukee, even Atlanta, with large Black communities in key swing states.
sentences.zh: 比如底特律、密尔沃基，甚至亚特兰大，这些关键摇摆州拥有大量黑人社区的城市。

sentences.en: Well, Maya, remind us of just how meaningful a problem Biden has with Black voters, according to all the data that you have been looking at.
sentences.zh: 那么，玛雅，根据你所查看的所有数据，请提醒我们拜登在黑人选民中面临的问题到底有多严重。
这是一个相当大的问题。

sentences.en: In 2020, President Biden won the election with about 87% of the Black vote.
sentences.zh: 2020年，拜登总统以约87%的黑人选票赢得了选举。

sentences.en: But polling that the Times has done found that at this stage, he only has about 71% of support from Black voters.
sentences.zh: 但《纽约时报》进行的民调发现，现阶段他仅获得约71%的黑人选民支持。
这是一个相当剧烈的下滑。
确实如此。

sentences.en: And what's even more concerning for Democrats is that former President Trump has actually increased his support among Black voters from 8% that he won in 2020
sentences.zh: 更让民主党人担忧的是，前总统特朗普实际上增加了他在黑人选民中的支持率，从2020年赢得的8%，

sentences.en: to about 22% that our poll found late last year.
sentences.zh: 上升到我们去年底民调发现的约22%。

sentences.en: It's a really striking drift away from Biden because a Republican presidential candidate has not topped more than 12% from Black voters in almost 50 years.
sentences.zh: 这种背离拜登的趋势非常惊人，因为在过去近50年里，没有一位共和党总统候选人在黑人选民中的支持率超过12%。

sentences.en: And so if former President Trump were to really have more than 20% support from Black voters, that would be a historic shift in Black voting behavior.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果前总统特朗普真的能获得超过20%的黑人选民支持，那将是黑人投票行为的历史性转变。
